sw19-s8.name: The one-sixteenth paragraph, step 8 from #321: "start gathering"
sw19-s8.text: That works out to about one-sixteenth of the grown-ups per child that our brains evolved with (Perry, 2023). So the emptiness you feel (the "Void") is real, since it's what that missing company feels like. Once you've de-armored, going back to a lonely life will tend to feel worse than it did with the armor on. So start gathering a tribe of people you're close to and see most days, or you'll eventually put the armor back on just to get through the loneliness.
sw19-s8.diagnosis: steps 6 and 7 (#320, #321) read every window High but the last sentence, Medium; the image change didn't move it; what a reader who lives alone could get wrong is that the tribe is something they must already have (the fit read of the post's version: "MISREAD: don't bother alone"); "start" says where they begin, one word
sw19-s8.decides: whether the last sentence reaches High; if so, the paragraph goes in
sw19-s8.first_fix: payoff: unchanged; join: unchanged; plain: "start gathering" says the act can begin now
